threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'Stokey' instead of Stoke Newington. Everyone here knows it's just Stokey, mate.
Last Saturday on the 59, a guy serenaded us with an old Beyoncé song. Must've rehearsed; he had all the moves, even spun the pole like a pro.

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy in a full suit skateboarding past a protest while juggling three apples. Only in Neukölln, right?

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Berlin can you catch a late-night U-Bahn with a DJ spinning in your car. It's like a secret rave on wheels.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a local by how they take the bus every day, ignoring the delays, while newcomers panic about BART's latest meltdown.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a suit singing to himself on the 22 Fillmore while a toddler directly across from him was silently staring, totally transfixed.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think they can just walk into a plaça and find a quiet moment, but Gràcia's plazas are basically living rooms — bustling, noisy, and always full of locals.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell by the way they take photos of the street signs like they’re rare artifacts, oblivious to the locals rushing past.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still say 'please' and 'thank you' to tube staff. Locals just nod and push past. Also, you look baffled when the train stops for no reason.
Heard a bloke on the 36 arguing with a seagull over chips near the market. Seagull won, flew off like it owned the place. Typical Peckham!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: The moment I smelled currywurst and saw a group of kids breakdancing on the sidewalk while an old Berliner fed the pigeons. That’s life here.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can find spontaneous street parties in the summer where locals whip out grills and blast music. It's like a pop-up festival every weekend.

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot locals by how they know to avoid the back of the BART during rush hour—it's like letting the tourists line up for the best view.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy on the 8X who could recite every line of Shakespeare while the bus lurched into a pothole. Must be a Tenderloin regular.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia is all about Gaudí, but they miss the hidden gems like local artisan shops tucked away on Carrer de Joan Blanques.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their bewilderment at the lack of escalators in the Diagonal metro stations—it's like a rite of passage.
